title: Luigi's Mansion
description: Nintendo's GameCube launch showcase (2001): Luigi wins a mansion he never entered in a contest he never entered, and hoovers its ghosts with the Poltergust 3000. This export is decoded straight from the disc: all 75 room shells assembled in mansion-global coordinates with every furniture piece at its jmp/furnitureinfo placement (click one to see the vacuum yank it open — the game's own .anm clip), the 72 doorways from the DOL's own door table with their swing clips held at the apex, and the seven-shot opening cutscene rebuilt as data — sets, envelope-skinned actors and per-frame cameras baked from the demo player's .scd/.sco channels.

assets.name: Chest of drawers
assets.description: The chest of drawers. Its two clips are the rest pose and the vacuum interaction — chest_1 is what plays when the Poltergust yanks the drawers.

assets.name: The mansion
assets.description: The whole mansion, streamed room by room. The storey areas peel the dollhouse: basement, ground floor, first floor, attic, and the exterior shells. Furniture placements come from Map/map2.szp jmp/furnitureinfo; doors from the door list in the game binary itself.

assets.name: Luigi — the forest walk
assets.description: Luigi's 338-frame forest walk: a 122-node model with 64 skinning envelopes, driven by opwf_luigi.key. The .sls face shapes are applied at rest; the .slk talking-flap weight tracks are not yet exported.

assets.name: The mansion approach
assets.description: The mansion approach set, 1.87 MB of facade — shared by five of the seven intro shots, with op_mansion.key swaying its trees.

assets.name: The mansion — the door opens
assets.description: The same facade driven by opod_mansion.key: the front door swings open for the final shot.

assets.name: The opening
assets.description: The opening cutscene's stage: the dark forest and the mansion approach with every intro actor. Play the script to watch the seven shots the game streams before the title — the cameras are the game's own hermite channels, baked per frame at 30 fps.
